title: Institutional holdings router for high-priority historical auction catalogues
purpose: Reduce dependence on commercial catalogue scans by locating institutional holdings and persistent catalogue series for scientific/model/natural-history sales that remain incompletely lot-indexed on the public web.

repositories.institution: William Andrews Clark Memorial Library, UCLA
repositories.scope: Auction catalogues from 1922 to 2024 from a wide range of auction houses

Exceptional Scientific and Engineering Works of Art Including The Alfred Schett Collection

repositories.research_value: Confirms institutional survival of exactly the scientific/model catalogue family prioritized in pass 16 and supplies stable sale codes/box locations without purchasing scans.
repositories.access_limit: No digitized catalogue body was exposed by the finding aid in this pass.

high_priority_series.title: Scientific and engineering works of art, instruments and models
Scientific, medical and engineering works of art
Exceptional scientific and engineering works of art: including natural history and the William L. Camp Jr spectacle collection
Scientific instruments, including the Josef Pieter Zallinger collection of scientific instruments and associated books by Georg Friedrich Brander and other eminent makers

repositories.research_value: The library holds a continuous Christie’s scientific-model catalogue sequence, including 1997-2001 and 2002-2006, rather than isolated sales. This is the strongest institutional route yet found for systematic full-catalogue screening of the South Kensington family.
repositories.access_limit: OPAC holdings are not equivalent to digitized full text; no remote scan entitlement is inferred.

christies_series_expansion.finding: The high-priority Christie’s scientific/model family extends beyond the sampled 1991/1997 records mapped in pass 16 and becomes increasingly explicit about natural history in the 2000s.

christies_series_expansion.priority_effect: The 2005 sales move to A+ because the catalogue titles explicitly combine scientific works/models and natural history, the exact overlap where provenance-lost Blaschka models are most likely to be catalogued outside maker indexes.

public_lot_archive_finding.christies: Christie's still exposes individual lot pages from historical Scientific and Engineering Works of Art sales, and some pages retain a 'More from' relation to the source sale.
public_lot_archive_finding.example: A 1998 astrolabe lot page explicitly cites the 8 April 1998 Exceptional Scientific and Engineering Works of Art, Instruments and Models catalogue and lot 50.
public_lot_archive_finding.search_implication: Before obtaining scans, search the surviving Christie's lot archive using object-class terms plus sale-title phrases. Maker-name searches alone returned no old physical Blaschka lot in the sampled scientific-model series.
public_lot_archive_finding.negative_guard: Search-engine absence from historical Christie's lot pages is not equivalent to browsing every lot in the sale.

access_strategy: Treat Museo Galileo 1997-2006 serial holdings as a potential batch-screening route rather than ordering isolated commercial scans.
Use UCLA Clark stable sale-code records to identify exact catalogues and box locations, especially MSI-8351 and MSI-9355.
Search institution OPACs for the exact Christie’s series titles before paying for scans.
Use surviving Christie's historical lot pages to reconstruct sale-level keywords and lot-number neighborhoods when indexed.
If remote scans are unavailable, record the institutional holding as a future archive/library target rather than converting metadata into a negative result.
next_targets: Museo Galileo: establish which individual issues exist within the 1997-2001 and 2002-2006 Christie’s runs and whether reproduction/remote consultation is possible.
Search UK institutional library catalogues for the same continuing-series titles, prioritizing London holdings.
Search Christie's lot archive for 2005 scientific/natural-history sale object classes: glass model, zoological model, anatomical model, jellyfish, sea anemone, coral, mollusc, worm, teaching model.
Retain 29 May 1997, 8 Apr 1998, 15 Apr 1999, 7 Apr 2005 and 29 Jun 2005 as the first full-catalogue screening sequence once scans can be accessed.
